provenance.note: synthetic; price rendered as an Arabic-Indic digit string instead of a JSON number. Originally authored expecting rejection ('no normalizer in this codebase maps Arabic-Indic digits') — corrected after running the benchmark: Python's stdlib decimal.Decimal actually parses Unicode decimal-digit categories natively (Decimal('١٢٩.٠٠') == Decimal('129.00')), so app_shared.money.parse_money accepts this string correctly through its normal Decimal(str) path. This is a genuinely useful finding surfaced BY running this benchmark against real code rather than assumption — the money boundary is more robust to Arabic-Indic input than its own docstring claims, and this case now documents that as a verified positive rather than an assumed gap.
